Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently attended the Startup School 2026 event, and her keynote speech video has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel. Please watch the video below.

Susan Kare shared wonderful stories and design insights.

It has been over 40 years since the original Macintosh was launched, yet the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look just as outstanding today as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare conceived for the original Macintosh still exist in macOS today in various forms—sometimes even in their original appearance. From the Command key symbol, the Happy Mac image at startup, the system fonts, to the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped Mac's visual language but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has studied Apple's history should have seen Kare's manuscripts, and even read or heard her interviews about her early work, hearing her firsthand share the passion and frustrations that shaped those early years—the era when the graphical user interface and bitmap images were still uncharted territory—is always particularly captivating.

Therefore, if you are interested in learning about design, understanding Apple's history, or simply want to hear an expert who loves and has dedicated her life to a certain field talk passionately about her craft, then Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple in detail, Kare also discussed how she joined the company, showcased her work after leaving Apple, and shared various anecdotes from Apple's early days, while quoting other legendary designers to bring everyone more inspiration.
